architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.tie_interpretation: The deterministic VOI layer is indifferent among the tied top experiments: they share an identical component vector. Tie-breaking is therefore a genuine task left to the Agent, and any selection inside this set cannot have been read off the VOI ranking.
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: After verifying modifier functionality and recalculating the NCO:OH stoichiometry, run at least two independent repeats. Accept support for H-RESIN over H-CORE if every repeat has SI_15_60 < 3.80% and the maximum minus minimum repeat value is <= 2.00 percentage points. The 3.80% boundary is half the 7.61% H-CORE linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Apply thresholds only when at least two repeats agree within 2.00 percentage points. If every repeat has SI_15_60 >= 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified because the result is at or above the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction. If every repeat has SI_15_60 < 3.80%, H-CORE is falsified at the declared 2.00% discrimination resolution. If repeat agreement is worse than 2.00 percentage points, neither hypothesis is falsified because the result is not reproducibly attributable to the formulation. This dual-axis composition cannot falsify H-RESIN versus H-DUAL separately.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run an acrylic-only composition at the same reactive mass fraction and matched realized viscosity state using M-HOLD-120, with verified modifier functionality, recalculated NCO:OH stoichiometry, and the same repeat-agreement rule, to separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured at 120 C over 15-60 minutes
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41 combines 15% acrylic-like modifier with 5% minor-tackifier-like modifier while retaining the direct 120 C matched-window drift measurement. It is intended to reduce the established viscosity-growth failure mode and tests suppression beyond the 7.61% reactive-core dilution prediction. The direct observable is interpretable, but conclusions are restricted to formulation-level rheology and do not distinguish resin-wide suppression from minor-tackifier specialization.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120 because it directly measures the declared failure mode, is in the deterministic tied top set, uses the smallest supported dual-axis intervention, and avoids extrapolation. I followed the Skeptic's interpretation rather than the proposer's stronger causal wording: H-RESIN and H-DUAL remain entangled, state variation is a major confounder, and functionality, stoichiometry, and repeat agreement must be verified before applying thresholds.

uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for the primary observable because the 120 C, 15-60 minute window is directly measured and matches the available reference window; formulation-level attribution remains limited by the dual-axis design.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: Direct SI_15_60 observation has no fit or extrapolation; the declared discrimination resolution is 2.00 percentage points, with at least two independent repeats required.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: High: prior 120 C E2 preparations showed a 3.5688-fold viscosity range and 0.5848 sample CV. Record process history, verify functionality, and require <=2.00 percentage-point repeat agreement, but M-HOLD-120 does not itself match the realized viscosity state.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence, with the magnitude of thermal-hold drift not attributable to reactive-core dilution alone.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C hold shows SI_15_to_60 of 9.51% for E1 versus 51.54% for E5, with SI_15_to_90 of 16.85% and 93.08%, respectively.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local time-domain evidence consists only of single original runs for E1 and E5, each with four measurements over 15-90 minutes, and contains no measured trajectory for the candidate modifier axes. In contrast, temperature response is sampled from 80-130 C in six-point sweeps with multiple E2 realizations. The large E2 viscosity-level spread is important process-state uncertainty, but the modifier-dependent time trajectory needed to separate H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL remains unmeasured.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity at 120 C at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes and report the matched-window SI_15_to_60 relative change.
Use at least two independent repeats with fully recorded preparation and thermal-history conditions so drift can be compared at a controlled realized viscosity state.

Include an acrylic-only composition and a composition with a non-zero minor tackifier axis, with reactive mass fraction recorded so each result can be compared with the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction.
Use the same measured time window and temperature for all compared compositions; do not extrapolate beyond the 15-60 minute window.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and a controlled realized viscosity state, does adding acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like modifier suppress 120 C isothermal drift beyond the linear-dilution prediction, and is the low-drift regime achieved only when the minor tackifier axis is non-zero?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN and H-DUAL cannot be separated because both modifier axes are active; an acrylic-only hold is required for that distinction.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, the result supports H-RESIN over H-CORE by showing suppression below half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. Because both modifier axes are present, it does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result is consistent with H-CORE's linear-dilution prediction; if SI_15_60 is below 3.80%, H-CORE is falsified at the declared 2.00% resolution.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between 3.80% and 7.61% would show neither the required superlinear suppression nor agreement with the declared low-drift acceptance boundary. It would therefore leave H-CORE versus H-RESIN unresolved at the preregistered resolution and would not adjudicate H-RESIN versus H-DUAL.

proposer.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured directly from the 120 C viscosity readings at 15 and 60 minutes

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI, but uses a higher acrylic-like modifier level without separating any additional hypothesis pair or improving measurement interpretability.
It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI, but imposes a larger 20% acrylic-like intervention burden while providing the same direct drift observable and hypothesis separation.
It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI, but its 22.5% acrylic-like loading is a larger intervention with no additional discrimination benefit.
It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI, but its 25% acrylic-like loading is the largest supported perturbation and adds no hypothesis separation relative to S1C41.
Its 7.5% minor-tackifier-like level lies outside the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4% cluster, adding extrapolation risk while preserving the same direct hold-drift discrimination.

proposer.reasoning: The failure mode is an unresolved 120 C isothermal time trajectory, and M-HOLD-120 measures that quantity directly without model fitting or extrapolation. S1C41 separates H-CORE from both modifier-suppression hypotheses at the declared 2.00% resolution, remains inside the externally supported 15% acrylic and 5% minor-tackifier regions, and is the smallest sufficient dual-axis intervention among the tied top cards.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI component vectors and therefore are scientifically tied in the deterministic layer. S1C41 is selected because its 15% acrylic-like and 5% minor-tackifier-like levels both lie in directly supported evidence regions while using the smallest total modifier burden. It preserves the same direct hold-drift discrimination as the higher-acrylic alternatives without adding an unsupported perturbation.

residual_decision_risk: The dual-axis formulation leaves H-RESIN and H-DUAL entangled.
Large realized-viscosity state variation may confound drift differences with preparation state.
Unverified modifier functionality could invalidate the assumed reactive mass fraction and NCO:OH stoichiometry.
Two repeats without a prespecified dispersion or disagreement rule may not support threshold-based falsification.
The small base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower of 0.004583 indicates limited score separation from the next strictly lower experiment, despite the unchanged top set under the tested sweep.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection identifies uncontrolled realized-viscosity state as a major confounder: the proposed M-HOLD-120 directly measures the relevant 120 C drift coordinate, but without state matching or a state-specific anchor, threshold crossings cannot uniquely support formulation-level falsification. This weakens causal interpretation and requires verified modifier functionality, recalculated stoichiometry, state matching or an anchor, and a prespecified repeat-agreement rule. It does not make M-ANCHOR preferable as the primary experiment because M-ANCHOR does not directly measure the declared failure mode. The proposal also correctly acknowledges that its dual-axis formulation cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold would be needed for that separate question, but this does not invalidate the primary dual-axis drift test.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is in the five-experiment tied top set. No tested perturbation of any individual weight term from 0.5x to 1.5x changes the tied top set; every recommendation_flip_boundary is null, and top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0. These perturbations are scientifically defensible as a local sensitivity range, but this establishes decision stability of the transparent VOI score, not scientific correctness or confidence.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The protocol can directly measure SI_15_60 and can numerically produce the stated thresholds of 3.80% and 7.61% for S1C41, so the criterion is operationally attainable. It is not sufficiently protected against process-state variation to serve as a strong formulation-level falsification criterion without additional state control and a prespecified repeat-dispersion rule.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low-drift result could support either resin-wide superlinear suppression or the specific claim that the minor tackifier axis is required; it cannot establish the H-DUAL specialization claim.
objections.objection: The proposer lists H-CORE, H-RESIN and H-DUAL as separated, but the dual-axis composition S1C41 has both AC1920 at 15% and TK100 at 5% active. Its predicted SI_15_60 values are identical for H-RESIN and H-DUAL at 3.804%, so H-RESIN versus H-DUAL remains completely entangled. The proposer does admit this in hypotheses_not_separated and in the outcome interpretation, but the separated-hypotheses label overstates coverage.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Suppression relative to the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction could reflect dilution, acrylic effects, tackifier effects, modifier interaction, or altered reaction stoichiometry rather than the claimed H-RESIN or H-DUAL mechanism.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes acrylic-like modifier content to 15% and minor-tackifier-like content to 5% simultaneously, while reducing the reactive core to a stated reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. Therefore any SI_15_60 change cannot be attributed to either modifier axis individually. In addition, the payload states that if either modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated, but the proposed formulation and protocol do not require verified functionality or an adjusted NCO:OH calculation.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A difference in SI_15_60 may be a preparation-state effect, and a failure to cross 3.80% or 7.61% cannot be confidently interpreted as evidence against H-CORE or H-RESIN.
objections.objection: The scientific question requires a controlled realized viscosity state, but M-HOLD-120 explicitly has controls_process_state=false and the proposed protocol only says to run at least two independent repeats with recorded preparation and thermal history. The original E2 data show a 3.5688-fold viscosity spread at 120 C across three preparations, with a sample CV of 0.5848. Recording process history does not itself match or control the realized state.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No major interpretability claim is lost for the numerical drift observable itself; the weakness lies in causal attribution, not in how SI_15_60 is computed.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 is directly calculated from viscosity readings at the matched 15 and 60 minute window. It does not require a model fit, extrapolation, or imputation, so this part of the proposal survives the attack.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could be declared to falsify H-CORE or H-RESIN based on a threshold crossing that is not reproducible or not attributable to the modifier composition.
objections.objection: The stated thresholds are numerically separated from the declared 2.00% resolution: for S1C41, H-CORE predicts 7.61% and the H-RESIN/H-DUAL acceptance boundary is 3.80%. However, the protocol provides only two repeats and does not specify a rule for repeat dispersion, confidence bounds, exclusion, or handling disagreement between repeats. Because process-state control is absent and the measured E2 state spread is large, the protocol can produce values below 3.80% or at/above 7.61%, but it cannot establish that the result is a formulation-level falsification rather than uncontrolled realization variation.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: There is no identified leakage-based invalidation, but molecular or chain-level conclusions would be unsupported if added after measurement.
objections.objection: No planned step uses the target formulation identity, wet-lab outcome, or outcome-derived label; the proposal is consistent with the stated outcome-blind policy. The registry also limits the hypotheses to formulation-level rheological mechanisms. The protocol therefore does not improperly claim that M-HOLD-120 establishes a molecular reaction pathway, although the mechanistic wording about encounter frequency should remain interpreted only as the registered formulation-level model.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add an acrylic-only composition at the same reactive mass fraction and matched process state, plus a no-tackifier dual-axis control if needed, to separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL. Require verified modifier functionality and recalculation of NCO:OH stoichiometry. Add a state-specific viscosity anchor or another prespecified realized-state matching criterion before the 120 C hold, and define how the two or more repeats must agree before applying the 3.80% and 7.61% thresholds.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The experiment claims inference at a controlled realized viscosity state, but M-HOLD-120 does not control that state. This is especially serious because the original E2 preparations show a 3.5688-fold viscosity range at 120 C and a 0.5848 sample CV. With both modifier axes active and no state-matching anchor or state-control design, a measured SI_15_60 threshold crossing cannot be uniquely attributed to the proposed formulation mechanism.

tool_trace.reason: Required first to load the upstream state-aware material structure, identify the relevant state-shift and calibration rules, and make subsequent candidate or experiment ranking admissible.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

voi_sent_to_model.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi_sent_to_model.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
